tour.title: When You Can't Pray: Grief, Lament, and God's Presence in Loss
tour.intro: Three weeks after losing your mother, prayer may feel like a door that won't open — or a language you've forgotten. This tour doesn't argue you out of that. It sits with you in it: six honest conversations about grief as love's shadow, about lament as the cry of faith rather than its absence, about God's silence in suffering, and about what prayer even is when you can't produce any. You'll hear people who have buried children, spouses, and parents talk about it without tidying it up.

steps.why: Start with permission to grieve exactly as you are. Jeff Jenkins, who lost his wife, insists "grief is not sinful," that "no two griefs are the same," and that nobody has the right to tell you where you should be in this — "nobody can do that and nobody should." He also names the clichés that will land on you ("God needed another angel") and how to let them pass without letting them define your grief.
steps.episodeTitle: Some Things I Wish Everyone Knew About Grief

steps.why: Tom Wright gives grief a theological home: "not to grieve is to deny love, because grief is the shadow side of love," and since the incarnate Jesus wept at the tomb of his friend, "it is perfectly honouring to God to lament." He tells of a widow who delayed her grief for years and the damage that did — a warning for anyone tempted to skip the sorrow in the name of hope.

This is your exact question, spoken by a woman who lost her father and can't pray: doubt makes prayer feel "silly," and her grief feels selfish. Wright answers, "This is not selfish and it is not unimportant. God loves your broken heart as much as he loved your unbroken heart before." He doesn't tell her to push through — he tells her to inhabit Gethsemane and the story of Mary and Martha, to say to Jesus "if you'd been here, my dad wouldn't have died," and to let the Psalms (even Psalm 88, "which leaves you in the dark, but with the knowledge that somehow it's God's darkness") be the prayer when you have none.
steps.episodeTitle: #52 ‘I wish I didn’t exist’. Pain and suffering Part 2

steps.why: Cameron Cole buried his three-year-old son, and he names the two temptations in grief: "to get bitter and turn away from God, or to fake it." His alternative is to "stay in the conversation" — suffering is "meant to be processed with your heavenly Father," and God "is inviting a prolonged conversation." The Psalm 22 language of "I feel like you're far away, but I know you're supposed to be good" is itself the prayer.

Here the hosts read Job's cursing of the day of his birth — the Bible showing you "how this sounds when someone is in this situation and they open their mouth." Their conclusion reframes everything: "You don't lament to a God that you think is not there... lament rather than being a signal of the absence of faith is actually a sign that faith is very much present." If you can't manage prayer, even a cry of "why" is faith doing its thing.

This closes the tour where you are standing: "God makes a promise and then he's silent through the exile and the suffering... a lot of times in our suffering it's that way too. We have a promise, and God suffers with us, but he's silent." The hosts are careful not to dress the silence up — God was silent in his own suffering — but they hold out that the promise was spoken on the front end: the God who goes into exile with you is the God who brings you home.
steps.episodeTitle: 40 Minutes In The Old Testament: Episode 57

tour.closing: Nobody in these six conversations tells you to hurry, to feel better, or to find the lesson. What they offer instead is company: the grief itself as evidence of love, the cry of lament as a form of faith, and a God who weeps at tombs, stays silent in exile, and keeps his promise anyway. When you can't pray, the Psalms can pray for you — and one day, in your own time, your voice may find its way back into them. Be gentle with yourself in these weeks. The love that is grieving is the love that was real.

caveats: Clips on ad-inserted hosts (Megaphone: ask-nt-wright, spoken-gospel) can land up to ~2 minutes off against today’s stream. This is a known corpus-wide drift, not a bug in this tour.
A tour is model output over machine transcripts. The "why" text should report what a transcript says; it is not a claim that the speaker is right.

The player streams each episode straight from its publisher. A few hosts (Substack’s CDN, for one) refuse hotlinked requests and the step will say so and offer the URL instead — the clip boundaries are still good, the playback path is not.
